title: Karl Mayer lines up new technology for ITMA Asia
title_ko: Karl Mayer, ITMA Asia의 신기술 라인업
summary: Karl Mayer will address the growing pressures on Asian textile manufacturers with a wide range of new machines and textile developments at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, complemented by a major product show at its manufacturing site in Changzhou. The company will have two stands at the exhibition, with warp knitting technologies […] The post Karl Mayer lines up new technology for ITMA Asia appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Karl Mayer will address the growing pressures on Asian textile manufacturers with a wide range of new machines and textile developments at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, complemented by a major product show at its manufacturing site in Changzhou. The company will have two stands at the exhibition, with warp knitting technologies in Hall 4.1 and warp preparation developments in Hall 3. Further machine premieres will be staged by Karl Mayer China at the Changzhou site. Asia remains central to Karl Mayer’s global strategy and is home to some of the world’s most dynamic textile manufacturing markets. Producers across the region, however, are facing rising labour, energy and financing costs alongside continued price pressure from international brands. Sustainability requirements, shorter lead times and smaller production runs are adding further pressure on margins. Close to customers Karl Mayer says its latest developments have been designed specifically to address these challenges through higher productivity, greater flexibility and improved resource efficiency. Karl Mayer CEO Lutz Wolf. © Karl Mayer “Our closeness to customers in Asia helps us identify market requirements at an early stage and translate them into targeted innovations,” says Karl Mayer CEO Lutz Wolf. “At this trade fair, we will be showcasing solutions that are not only technologically leading, but above all, deliver measurable added value and long-term growth opportunities for our customers.” Warp knitting In warp knitting, Karl Mayer will introduce a new generation of tricot machines building on the cost-effective range that has proved particularly successful in China from the late 2010s onwards. content: A first-of-its kind Circular Textile Lab aims to prevent ‘virgin textile waste’ from reaching the landfills. The lab will convert textile discards into useful and creative products through a circular, skills-based approach, train women from underprivileged communities and provide opportunities to develop sustainable livelihoods by reusing and transforming textile waste. An initiative of Bengaluru South City Corporation, the city’s first Circular Textile Lab and Solid Waste Management (SWM) Learning Centre, will be inaugurated at the ward-level integrated SWM Centre, in Koramangala on Monday, aimed at promoting sustainable waste management and reducing the amount of waste sent to landfills. The Circular Textile Lab, located in the same facility, will address the growing problem of virgin textile waste reaching landfills. Photo | EPS The SWM Learning Centre is being established as a practical learning and capacity-building facility for school and college students, citizens, corporate employees, government personnel, NGOs and SWM workers. Located within an operational waste management facility that processes 18 tonnes of different waste streams daily, the centre will combine classroom learning with first-hand exposure to waste processing. Through interactive programmes, demonstrations, games and facility tours, participants will learn about waste segregation, the seven R’s of sustainability, composting, dry and reject waste management, zero-waste campuses and events, and ways to reduce waste at source. The Circular Textile Lab, located in the same facility, will address the growing problem of virgin textile waste reaching landfills. summary: Pangaia has renewed its collaboration with Italian yarn producer Fulgar, selecting its EVO bio-based yarn for the international brand’s Seamless Activewear Fall-Winter 2026 collection. The new collection is the first to be developed by Pangaia’s Milan-based design studio and sees EVO return as one of the key materials in the activewear capsule, following its use […] The post Pangaia renews Fulgar yarn choice appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Pangaia has renewed its collaboration with Italian yarn producer Fulgar, selecting its EVO bio-based yarn for the international brand’s Seamless Activewear Fall-Winter 2026 collection. The new collection is the first to be developed by Pangaia’s Milan-based design studio and sees EVO return as one of the key materials in the activewear capsule, following its use in the line introduced in 2025. The continued partnership reflects Pangaia’s confidence in the performance characteristics of Fulgar’s 100% bio-based yarn, which has been developed to meet growing demand for high-performance materials produced from renewable resources. EVO is produced from 50% renewable feedstocks, including castor oil sourced from crops grown on arid land that does not compete with food production, and 50% industrial corn not intended for human consumption. According to Fulgar, the resulting yarn combines lightweight comfort and technical performance with the use of renewable raw materials. The yarn’s properties are particularly suited to activewear applications. Lightweight, breathable, elastic and quick-drying, EVO enables garments to move naturally with the body while providing effective compression, softness and freedom of movement. Its thermoregulating and bacteriostatic properties are also designed to support lasting wearer comfort. © Fulgar These characteristics have been incorporated into Pangaia’s latest Seamless Activewear capsule, which represents an evolution of the collection first introduced in 2025. The Fall-Winter 2026 range features more refined construction, graduated compression and an enhanced second-skin fit designed to support natural body movement. title: Netherlands Embassy delegation visits 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd
title_ko: 네덜란드 대사관 대표단, 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd 방문
summary: Strengthening Partnerships for a Sustainable & Responsible Garment Industry 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd., a LEED Platinum-rated green factory of TEAM Group, welcomed a high-level delegation from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bangladesh, Solidaridad Network Asia, and Fair Wear Foundation today. The delegation included Mrs. Janna van der Linden, Deputy Ambassador and […] The post Netherlands Embassy delegation visits 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Strengthening Partnerships for a Sustainable & Responsible Garment Industry 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd., a LEED Platinum-rated green factory of TEAM Group, welcomed a high-level delegation from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bangladesh, Solidaridad Network Asia, and Fair Wear Foundation today. The delegation included Mrs. Janna van der Linden, Deputy Ambassador and Head of Trade & Development Cooperation, alongside representatives from the Embassy, Solidaridad Network Asia and Fair Wear Foundation. The delegation was welcomed by Mr. Abdullah Hil Nakib, DMD, TEAM Group, together with the leadership team of 4A Yarn Dyeing and TEAM Group Sustainability. During the visit, the delegation explored 4A’s approach to responsible business, sustainable manufacturing, digital transformation, environmental performance, decarbonisation efforts, implementing circular economy, and preparedness for evolving EU regulatory requirements. The visit reflects the growing importance of collaboration among industry, development partners and stakeholders in advancing responsible, competitive and sustainable garment manufacturing in Bangladesh. TEAM Group remains committed to going beyond compliance—building a resilient, responsible and future-ready textile industry. title: SQ Group wins three honors for ESG excellence
summary: Two Gold Awards and a Jury’s Special Award recognize progress in ESG strategy, Women’s leadership and Workforce development When SQ Group began its journey in 1993, ESG was not yet part of the vocabu...
content: Two Gold Awards and a Jury’s Special Award recognize progress in ESG strategy, Women’s leadership and Workforce development When SQ Group began its journey in 1993, ESG was not yet part of the vocabulary of Bangladesh’s apparel industry. More than three decades later, both the business and the industry around it have been transformed. Figure: The Group photo at Bangladesh’s inaugural ESG Excellence Awards, where SQ Group received three honors across three distinct areas. Today, SQ Group is the Bangladesh manufacturing arm of Singapore-headquartered Q Collection, with operations spanning knitwear through SQ Celsius, lingerie and activewear through SQ Birichina, and vertically integrated capabilities through SQ Hues. That evolution was recognized at Bangladesh’s inaugural ESG Excellence Awards, where SQ Group received three honors across three distinct areas: Two Gold Awards as Sector Leader - for ESG Strategy & Policy Implementation and Gender Equity & Women Leadership Advancement - and the Jury’s Special Award for Skills Development & Workforce Upskilling. The breadth of the recognition matters. Global customers increasingly expect their manufacturing partners to deliver not only price, quality, and speed, but also stronger environmental performance, responsible workplaces, greater transparency, and a workforce equipped for a more technology-driven industry. SQ Group’s three awards touch each of these priorities. ESG beyond compliance The Gold Award for Excellence in ESG Strategy & Policy Implementation recognised the Group’s work to strengthen ESG governance and implement its Environmental and Social Management System across its operations, alongside investments in energy efficiency and renewable energy. title: Egypt’s garment exports reach $2.14B in first seven months of 2026
summary: Egypt’s ready-made garment exports increased 14 percent year on year during the first seven months of 2026, reaching $2.14 billion, compared with $1.869 billion during the same period in 2025, according to data from the Ready-Made Garments Export Council.The sector recorded an increase of approximately $270 million compared with the previous year. In July alone, […] The post Egypt’s garment exports reach $2.14B in first seven months of 2026 appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Egypt’s ready-made garment exports increased 14 percent year on year during the first seven months of 2026, reaching $2.14 billion, compared with $1.869 billion during the same period in 2025, according to data from the Ready-Made Garments Export Council. The sector recorded an increase of approximately $270 million compared with the previous year. In July alone, garment exports rose 19 percent to around $380 million, up from $320 million in July 2025, according to the council’s monthly report. Egyptian-owned companies contributed 62.5 percent of total garment exports between January and July, generating $1.337 billion, compared with $1.163 billion a year earlier, marking a 15 percent annual increase. Exports from foreign-invested companies also grew 14 percent to $802 million, compared with $705 million in the same period last year, accounting for 37.5 percent of total sector exports. The number of Egyptian exporting companies rose to 749 during the seven-month period, up from 722 a year earlier, while the number of foreign-invested exporters rose to 115 from 106. Fadel Marzouk, Chairman of the Ready-Made Garments Export Council, said European markets remained the largest regional destination for Egyptian garment exports. Shipments to Europe surged 46 percent to $930 million, compared with $636 million in the first seven months of 2025, representing nearly 43 percent of total sector exports. Spain recorded the strongest growth among European markets, with exports rising 86 percent to $185 million. It was followed by the United Kingdom, up 69 percent to $86 million; Italy, up 51 percent to $55 million; France, up 45 percent to $48 million; and Germany, up 37 percent to $117 million. summary: In light of the decision of the Inter-Ministerial Committee formed by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, the National Board of Revenue (NBR), through Order No. 51/2026/Customs/519 dated 7 September 2026, has withdrawn Bond facilities for the import of 10–30 count cotton yarn under HS Headings 5205, 5206 and 5207. At the same time, genuine exporters have […] The post BTMA Statement on De-bonding of 10–30 Count Cotton Yarn Imports appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: In light of the decision of the Inter-Ministerial Committee formed by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, the National Board of Revenue (NBR), through Order No. 51/2026/Customs/519 dated 7 September 2026 , has withdrawn Bond facilities for the import of 10–30 count cotton yarn under HS Headings 5205, 5206 and 5207 . At the same time, genuine exporters have been allowed to import such yarn subject to prescribed conditions and the submission of a Bank Guarantee . The Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) considers this decision timely and appropriate to protect the domestic textile industry, particularly the spinning sector, and to prevent misuse of the Bond facility. BTMA sincerely appreciates and thanks the Government and the National Board of Revenue for taking this important initiative. 1. Revitalizing the Domestic Textile and Spinning Sector The import of yarn under Bond facilities has, for a long time, affected the demand for locally produced 10–30 count cotton yarn and limited the utilization of domestic spinning mill capacity. The new decision is expected to increase demand for locally produced yarn, create opportunities for closed and partially closed mills to resume operations, generate significant employment, and improve prospects for recovering investments made by banks and financial institutions. It is also expected to significantly reduce non-performing loans (NPLs) in the banking sector. 2. Increasing Value Addition and Conserving Foreign Currency Greater use of domestically produced yarn will significantly increase local value addition across the textile and RMG value chain while reducing foreign currency expenditure on imported yarn. summary: 국내 화장품 시장의 진입 문턱은 낮아졌지만 성장 문턱은 오히려 높아지고 있다. OEM·ODM 산업의 발달로 자체 생산시설 없이도 브랜드를 출시할 수 있게 되면서 시장에 뛰어드는 사업자는 급증했지만, 실제 일정 규모 이상으로 성장하는 과정에서는 자본과 유통, 물류, 마케팅 역량의 중요성이 더 커지고 있다.식품의약품안전처 등에 따르면 국내 화장품 책임판매업체 수는 2025년 2만8412개로 집계됐다. 같은 기간 화장품 제조업체는 4158개로 집계됐다.시장 참여자가 빠르게 늘어난 것과 달리 산업 자체의 성장 속도는 상대적으로 완만했다.

title: Palmal Group to develop flagship sustainable composite factory in Sylhet
title_ko: Palmal Group, Sylhet에 지속 가능한 주력 복합소재 공장 개발
summary: Palmal Group is developing Hamza Knit Dyeing Mills Ltd. at Sreehatta Economic Zone, Sylhet. The flagship composite facility marks a major investment in sustainable, future‑ready manufacturing for Ban...
content: Palmal Group is developing Hamza Knit Dyeing Mills Ltd. at Sreehatta Economic Zone, Sylhet. The flagship composite facility marks a major investment in sustainable, future‑ready manufacturing for Bangladesh. The new facility is being designed with sustainability at its core, with an ambition to achieve LEED Platinum certification. It will incorporate advanced technologies aimed at improving energy and water efficiency, reducing emissions and minimizing environmental impact. Figure 1: Land Lease Agreement Handed over to Palmal Management by Invest Bangladesh Authority, IBA. The planned factory will feature rooftop solar power generation, biomass boilers and an advanced Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) with water recycling facilities. It will also use energy- and water-efficient machinery, low-emission technologies and other sustainable manufacturing solutions. The Land Lease Agreement for the project was formally signed and handed over by Saleh Ahmed, Executive Member (Investment Development), BEZA and Additional Secretary, to Adnan Imtiaz Majid, Director, Central Management, Palmal Group. Figure 2: Officials from the companies/ The new facility is expected to further strengthen Palmal Group’s manufacturing capabilities while supporting its broader commitment to responsible production, resource efficiency and environmental sustainability. With sustainability integrated into the project from its foundation, Hamza Knit Dyeing Mills Ltd. is expected to emerge as a benchmark for green and resource-efficient manufacturing in Bangladesh. The investment reflects Palmal Group’s continued efforts to develop modern manufacturing infrastructure that combines industrial growth with environmental responsibility.

title: Memorandum of Understanding Signed Between WaterAid Bangladesh and BKMEA on Sustainable Water Management in the Knitwear Sector
summary: WaterAid Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to promote efficient and sustainable water use in Bangladesh’s knitwear sector and improve access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services for factory workers and surrounding communities. The MoU was signed at the BKMEA office in […] The post Memorandum of Understanding Signed Between WaterAid Bangladesh and BKMEA on Sustainable Water Management in the Knitwear Sector appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: WaterAid Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to promote efficient and sustainable water use in Bangladesh’s knitwear sector and improve access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services for factory workers and surrounding communities. The MoU was signed at the BKMEA office in Dhaka on Monday, 7 September 2026, by Azman Ahmed Chowdhury, Country Director of WaterAid Bangladesh, and Mohammad Rashed , Vice President of BKMEA, on behalf of their respective organisations. Mostafizur Rahman, Senior Programme Officer at the Embassy of Sweden in Bangladesh, attended the ceremony. BKMEA was represented by Engr. Md. Belayet Hossain Ripon, Director, and Farzana Sharmin, Joint Secretary of the Compliance Cell. Representatives from WaterAid Bangladesh included Partha Hefaz Sek, Director of Programmes and Policy Advocacy; Md. Mamun Chowdhury, Programme Coordinator; Plabon Gangopadhyay, Communications Coordinator; A.K.M. Masum Ul Alam, Water Governance and System Stewardship Specialist; Farah Naznin, Project Engineer; and Sing Mong Pru Marma, Communications Officer. Under the MoU, the two organisations will explore the development of a sustainable water-management plan for the knitwear sector. Priority areas include reducing unnecessary water consumption, minimising dependence on groundwater through alternative sources, adopting water-efficient technologies, recycling and reusing wastewater, harvesting and conserving rainwater, and identifying financing opportunities for sustainable water solutions. title: Chinese Manufacturing Is Coming to Bangladesh. Can Dhaka Turn It Into Industrial Power?
title_ko: 중국 제조업이 Bangladesh에 오고 있습니다. 다카가 이를 산업 발전으로 바꿀 수 있을까요?
summary: The arrival of Chinese manufacturers could help Bangladesh diversify beyond RMG and reduce some import dependence—but without local suppliers, skills, and technology transfer, the country may simply become another assembly base in China’s global supply chain For decades, Bangladesh’s economic relationship with China has been remarkably simple: China makes, Bangladesh imports. That relationship is now […] The post Chinese Manufacturing Is Coming to Bangladesh. Can Dhaka Turn It Into Industrial Power? appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: The arrival of Chinese manufacturers could help Bangladesh diversify beyond RMG and reduce some import dependence—but without local suppliers, skills, and technology transfer, the country may simply become another assembly base in China’s global supply chain For decades, Bangladesh’s economic relationship with China has been remarkably simple: China makes, Bangladesh imports . That relationship is now taking on another dimension. Chinese manufacturers are increasingly exploring production in Bangladesh, particularly in textiles and apparel, while Chinese businesses already have a significant presence in infrastructure, energy, telecommunications and other industrial activities. The significance goes well beyond the value of individual factory investments. Bangladesh exported US$48.28 billion in merchandise in FY2024-25, according to the Export Promotion Bureau, of which US$39.35 billion came from RMG . At the same time, China remains Bangladesh’s largest import source, with Bangladesh importing roughly US$24 billion worth of goods from China in FY2023-24 against exports of around US$1 billion . In other words, Bangladesh’s trade relationship with China carries a deficit of roughly US$23 billion . Chinese manufacturing investment could change that equation—from China selling to Bangladesh to China investing in Bangladesh to produce for Bangladesh and the world . But whether that is a transformation or simply a change of location depends on how much of the resulting value Bangladesh can retain. The investment opportunity is bigger than RMG The obvious entry point is apparel. title: Nordic apparel market makes traceability a sourcing priority
title_ko: 북유럽 의류 시장에서는 추적성을 소싱 우선순위로 삼고 있습니다.
summary: Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden) are becoming an important testing ground for Europe’s textile transition. Traceability is moving from a sustainability goal to a sourci...
content: Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden) are becoming an important testing ground for Europe’s textile transition. Traceability is moving from a sustainability goal to a sourcing requirement. Figure: Global fiber production reached 132 million tons in 2024. Less than 1% came from pre- and post-consumer textile recycling. The EU launched its Digital Product Passport (DPP) Registry on 20 July 2026. Textile-specific requirements are expected to follow under the EU’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation. The rules are expected to require data on fiber content, recycled materials, material origin, chemicals, durability and end-of-life options, according to the European Commission. Nordic brands are already preparing. H&M Group sourced from nearly 800 apparel factories in 23 countries and about 550 raw-material factories in 15 countries as of February 2026. In 2025, 91% of its materials were recycled or sustainably sourced. Recycled materials reached 32%, above its 30% target, according to H&M Group. Supplier certification is also growing. Almost 50% of H&M’s contracted apparel factories had Recycled Claim Standard certification. Another 39% had Global Recycled Standard certification. About 38.5% had Organic Content Standard certification, according to Shenglu Fashion. The focus is also moving deeper into the supply chain. Danish brand GANNI plans to cover all Tier 1, Tier 1+ and Tier 2 suppliers through social audits or assessments by 2028, according to GANNI’s 2026 sustainability strategy. This creates a clear message for global suppliers. Traceability will increasingly influence market access and sourcing decisions. content: RE&UP Recycling Technologies’ Next-Gen Cotton is being used in a new collection from Zalando’s private labels, marking a further step towards bringing textile-to-textile recycled fibres into mainstream commercial fashion production. Launched on Zalando in August, the collection comprises five T-shirts across YOURTURN by Zalando and Even&Odd by Zalando. The garments are made from a circular knitted fabric combining 80% organic cotton with 20% RE&UP Next-Gen Cotton, a recycled fibre produced from textile waste. The collection marks the first time RE&UP recycled fibres have featured in Zalando’s private label assortment and demonstrates how textile-to-textile recycling technologies can move beyond pilot projects into commercial-scale applications. As the fashion industry seeks to scale textile-to-textile recycling, RE&UP says it is developing the infrastructure required to support larger volumes and enable brands to integrate next-generation fibres into existing supply chains without compromising product quality. RE&UP’s proprietary recycling process transforms pre- and post-consumer textile waste through sorting, deconstruction and decolourisation. Between August 2025 and July 2026, the country shipped 3,373,941 tons of the fibre, 19% more than in the previous cycle, and reached […] The post Brazil sets new cotton export record appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Brazil ended the 2025/26 commercial year with a new record, consolidating its position as the world’s largest cotton exporter, according to ComexStat data compiled by the Brazilian Association of Cotton Growers (Abrapa). Between August 2025 and July 2026, the country shipped 3,373,941 tons of the fibre, 19% more than in the previous cycle, and reached record export revenue of US$5.3 billion. The result represents a milestone in Brazil’s expansion in the international market and reinforces the country’s role as a strategic supplier to the global textile industry. The increase represents approximately 538,500 additional tons of Brazilian cotton sold abroad and export revenues were 9% above the 2024/25 result. The result is the consequence of a transformation built over several years, driven by increased production and advances in different attributes of Brazilian cotton. “Brazil has expanded its production and gained scale, while also making progress in quality, traceability and sustainability,” said Danyella Bonfim, market intelligence and analysis coordinator at Abrapa. “This combination has strengthened the competitiveness of Brazilian cotton and, above all, the confidence of international buyers in the country’s ability to supply the market on a regular and consistent basis.” © Albrapa The performance kept Brazil at the top of the global cotton export rankings. According to data from the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) presented in Abrapa’s August report, the United States ranked second in 2025/26, with 2.656 million tons, followed by Australia, with 1.241 million tons. The 685-acre site was originally earmarked for […] The post BPDB plans 442 MW solar plant on unused Rampal site appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: The Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) plans to build a 442 MW solar power plant on unused land adjacent to the 1,320 MW Rampal thermal station in Bagerhat, at an estimated cost of BDT 24.98 billion. BPDB recently submitted its Development Project Proposal (DPP) to the Planning Commission. The 685-acre site was originally earmarked for the second phase of the Rampal coal plant but lay idle after the previous Awami League government adopted a policy against building new coal-fired power stations. BPDB now plans to install the 442 MW DC solar plant on the site. The coal-based power plant located in Rampal Upazila of Bagerhat | Photo: BPDB Work is scheduled to run from September of the current 2026–27 fiscal year to June 2029. BPDB will provide BDT 3.74 billion from its own resources, while the remaining BDT 21.24 billion will come from the Power Sector Development Fund. The estimate is based on an exchange rate of BDT 123 to the US dollar. The 1,320 MW coal plant at Rampal is operational and run by Bangladesh-India Friendship Power Company Limited (BIFPCL), a joint venture equally owned by India’s state-owned NTPC and Bangladesh’s BPDB. Policy approval for the adjacent solar project was granted at a ministerial meeting after the Planning Commission sought clearance from Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury. Two senior Industry and Energy Division officials told Bonik Barta on condition of anonymity that the division sought the minister’s clearance because of past controversies surrounding the Rampal plant. Verbal approval was granted, but a Project Evaluation Committee (PEC) meeting has yet to be held, they said. title: Making PFAS compliance possible for the European textile industry
summary: EURATEX supports the objective of reducing PFAS emissions and accelerating the transition towards safer and more sustainable alternatives. The European textile and apparel industry has already made significant progress in reducing PFAS use and continues to invest in substitution wherever technically feasible. However, an effective EU PFAS restriction for textiles must also be measurable, enforceable… Read more The post Making PFAS compliance possible for the European textile industry appeared first on EURATEX .
content: EURATEX supports the objective of reducing PFAS emissions and accelerating the transition towards safer and more sustainable alternatives. The European textile and apparel industry has already made significant progress in reducing PFAS use and continues to invest in substitution wherever technically feasible. However, an effective EU PFAS restriction for textiles must also be measurable, enforceable and workable in practice. Setting legal limits alone is not enough: companies, laboratories and enforcement authorities need clear rules on how compliance should be tested, how analytical results should be interpreted and how unavoidable background contamination should be treated. In its new position paper, “Making PFAS compliance possible for the European textile industry” , EURATEX identifies four essential conditions for successful implementation: analytical readiness, legal certainty, compatibility with circularity and regulatory coherence . Among its key recommendations, EURATEX calls for a tiered compliance approach, starting with Total Fluorine screening and moving to more targeted PFAS testing only where scientifically justified. Regulatory thresholds should reflect validated analytical capabilities and measurement uncertainty, while compliance rules should distinguish between intentional PFAS use and unavoidable background or cross-contamination. Particular attention is also needed for recycled textile materials . Legacy PFAS may remain in products manufactured years before current restrictions existed. EURATEX therefore calls for a coherent approach that protects textile-to-textile recycling while preventing new intentional PFAS inputs. title: Driving circularity with Uster recycled fiber matrix

summary: The two-way street for assessing mechanically recycled materials The textile industry’s commitment to circularity continues to accelerate, and mechanical recycling is viewed as a targeted approach to...
content: The two-way street for assessing mechanically recycled materials The textile industry’s commitment to circularity continues to accelerate, and mechanical recycling is viewed as a targeted approach to cutting textile waste and its environmental impact. At the forefront of this drive, Uster has developed the Recycled Fiber Matrix, a two-dimensional assessment of mechanically recycled fibers to guide optimum processing and end-uses. Figure 1: Uster Recycled Fiber Matrix for mechanically recycled cotton based on L(n) and SFC(n) Recycled cotton fibers are difficult to categorize because of their inconsistency and variability. How can the industry evaluate mechanically recycled material accurately – and match it to the most suitable spinning methods and product end-uses? Help is at hand from Uster, in the form of the Recycled Fiber Matrix. It provides an objective assessment of recycled cotton, so that recyclers, spinners and brands are guided towards what can be made from it, and how. The concept fits perfectly with the industry’s need for greater circularity and transparency in recycling. The facts that matter Precise data about the physical characteristics of recycled fibers is essential to understand how they will behave in spinning and their end-use. The Uster Recycled Fiber Matrix focuses on the essential numbers – such as length of fibers (L(n)), of the longest 5% fibers (5% L(n)), and short fiber content (SFC(n)). The background to the development of the Recycled Fiber Matrix involved testing of a significant number of 100% mechanically recycled cotton fiber samples from key recycling regions, including China, India and Europe. The new UltraView60 provides the same colour assessment technology […] The post VeriVide expands its LED colour assessment range appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: VeriVide – a member of the British Textile Machinery Association (BTMA) – is expanding its UltraView range of visual colour assessment equipment with the launch of a new compact model designed to make tuneable LED technology accessible to more organisations across textile and apparel supply chains. The new UltraView60 provides the same colour assessment technology and functionality as VeriVide’s existing UltraView system, but in a smaller and more cost-effective format for businesses that do not require a large viewing area or where laboratory space is limited. At the same time, the existing UltraView has been renamed UltraView90, creating a two-model range based around different viewing areas while retaining identical core technology and capabilities. The development comes as brands, textile manufacturers, suppliers and testing laboratories increasingly transition from conventional fluorescent lighting to LED technology for the visual assessment of colour. Fundamental consistency Consistent lighting conditions are fundamental to colour evaluation throughout textile supply chains, particularly where materials and finished products may be assessed at several different locations before reaching the consumer. Changes in lighting technology therefore need to be introduced consistently if manufacturers and their customers are to avoid discrepancies in colour approval. VeriVide, based in Leicester, UK, has specialised in controlled lighting and colour assessment for more than 60 years and developed the UltraView range to provide greater flexibility as specifications continue to evolve. content: Key global recycled fiber market projections Global production: Reached 132 million tons in 2024, with recycled fiber holding a 7.6% market share. Textile-to-Textile bottleneck: Less than 1% of global fiber comes from recycled textiles, as 98% of recycled polyester relies on plastic bottles. China market growth: Projected to grow from $3.32 billion to $5.87 billion by 2030. United States market growth: Projected to grow from $2.41 billion to $4.13 billion by 2030. India waste recovery: Recovers over 95% of its 7.07 million tons of annual pre-consumer textile waste, targeting a $3.5 billion market by 2030. Figure: According to Grand View Research, the US recycled polyester market stood at $2.41 billion and is projected to reach $4.13 billion by 2030. The global recycled fiber market is moving into a strategic phase. Brands are increasing recycled-content sourcing, governments are tightening circularity rules, and textile manufacturers are investing in recycling capacity. However, the demand for recycled fiber is soaring, while the supply of high-quality textile waste remains severely limited. According to the Materials Market Report by Textile Exchange, global fiber production reached a record high of 132 million tons in 2024. Recycled fibers accounted for only 7.6% of overall output. Recycled polyester remained the dominant recycled material, making up roughly 6.9% of the total fiber market. About 98% of recycled polyester was still sourced from plastic bottles. Recent 2026 data from Textile Exchange emphasizes that breaking this bottleneck requires shifting away from open-loop bottle recycling toward localized, renewable-powered textile-to-textile processing. The audit focused specifically on down processing, using […] The post A lighter footprint for down appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Allied Feather + Down, headquartered in Montebello, California, has announced the results of a recent carbon footprint audit conducted by Green Threads DPP at its facility in Hangzhou, China. The results show that Allied’s cradle-to-gate down processing generates 85% less carbon emissions than the estimated industry average. The audit focused specifically on down processing, using actual facility and supply chain data to quantify its carbon footprint. The result gives brands a more specific benchmark for evaluating the carbon impact of the down they source and the processes used to prepare it for finished products. “We’ve known for years that down plays an important role in building a more circular and lower-impact apparel value chain,” said Daniel Uretsky, president of Allied Feather + Down. “These audited results allow us to put real numbers behind that belief. The data shows that our processing methods deliver a dramatically lower carbon footprint than other down providers, giving brands objective information they can use when making material decisions.” The audit found that Allied’s processing methods generated 0.48 kg CO₂e per kg of down – about 85% lower than estimated industry averages (3.2 kg CO2e per kg) for conventional down and 57.9% lower than published figures (1.14 kg CO2e per kg) for recycled down. It also found that the carbon footprint of Allied’s down is 95% lower than the estimated carbon footprint of polyester fibres used in alternative insulations. Allied’s Hangzhou facility utilises on-site water reclamation, allowing 95% of all water to be reused, with only around 5% lost to evaporation. content: Terrot Textilmaschinen will showcase its latest circular knitting technology at the 24th Egypt Stitch & Tex Expo, taking place from 24-27 September 2026 at the Cairo International Conference Center (CICC) in Nasr City, Cairo. The German textile machinery specialist, a member of Santoni China Group, will participate together with its Egyptian representative Setraco Safouh Tex, presenting the Terrot I3P 196 open-width circular knitting machine. Designed to support flexible, high-quality production, the I3P 196 addresses applications ranging from sportswear, leisurewear and fashion to technical textiles, automotive fabrics and home textiles. Terrot says the exhibition will provide an important platform to engage with manufacturers, investors and industry partners from Egypt and neighbouring textile markets, as producers respond to shorter product development cycles, sustainability requirements and growing demand for differentiated fabrics. The I3P 196 being demonstrated in Cairo is configured with a 34-inch diameter, E24 gauge and 108 feeders. The production example features a double-face fabric structure, demonstrating the machine’s ability to process material combinations for versatile, performance-oriented textile applications. “Egypt and the wider region continue to offer important opportunities for textile manufacturing, investment and technological development,” said Martin Vorsatz, CEO of Terrot Textilmaschinen. “Together with Setraco, we are demonstrating how advanced circular knitting technology can help manufacturers combine product versatility with efficient and reliable production.” The I3P 196 has been developed for manufacturers requiring flexibility when producing knitted fabrics for multiple applications, allowing producers to respond to changing customer r

title: France turns textile EPR into a test of fashion’s business model
summary: France is taking textile EPR into a new phase. Brands will pay more when their business models contribute to faster textile waste. Figure: The EU’s revised Waste Framework Directive requires member s...
content: France is taking textile EPR into a new phase. Brands will pay more when their business models contribute to faster textile waste. Figure: The EU’s revised Waste Framework Directive requires member states to establish textile EPR schemes by April 2028. The shift became clearer on September 1, 2026, when France’s new “industrial and commercial practices” penalty took effect. Under the measure, certain products can face additional EPR charges based on the breadth of a company’s product range and the incentives it provides for repair. The penalty sits alongside France’s existing bonus-malus system for durability, recycled content and recyclability. The timing is significant. France has operated mandatory textile EPR since 2007, giving it almost two decades of experience. Yet collection remains far below ambition. About 32% of textiles placed on the market were collected in 2023, against a target of 60% by 2028. That gap exposes the harder side of circularity, and funding collection does not automatically create profitable recycling capacity. Refashion, France’s textile EPR organization, collected around 272,000 tons of clothing and footwear in 2025. But the industry still faces challenges in sorting, reuse and textile-to-textile recycling, where economics and available infrastructure remain critical constraints. The EU’s revised Waste Framework Directive requires member states to establish textile EPR schemes by April 2028. France’s model is one of the most developed real-world references for that transition. Material choices, product durability, recyclability, and repairability will increasingly influence the cost of putting garments on the European market. The first segment of the day featured the final rounds of the Case Catalyst and Public Speaking competitions. title: Meeting between ZDHC & BKMEA took place to accelerate sustainable chemical management in Bangladesh
summary: The Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) and the ZDHC Foundation held a strategic discussion recently on strengthening sustainable chemical management and reducing indus...
content: The Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) and the ZDHC Foundation held a strategic discussion recently on strengthening sustainable chemical management and reducing industrial water pollution across Bangladesh’s knitwear and textile manufacturing sector. The meeting focused on a proposed 36-month initiative designed to support factories in adopting practical chemical management systems, improving wastewater performance, and building stronger environmental practices. Amin & Jahan Corporation Ltd. and ECOPSIS also joined the discussion as implementation partner and solution providers. Figure 1: BKMEA leaders meet ZDHC and solution providers. During the meeting, BKMEA Vice President, Mohammad Rashed stressed the importance of establishing clear and objective criteria for selecting participating factories so that the initiative can deliver measurable improvements. He also highlighted the potential of shared environmental infrastructure, including zone-wise Central Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs), to address common wastewater challenges. BKMEA Director, Minhazul Hoque emphasized that the initiative should prioritize hands-on capacity building and technical support for factories rather than creating additional audit or compliance burdens. He noted that practical guidance and factory-level assistance would be essential for achieving meaningful and sustainable improvements. title: All About AI: Brian Lindauer of VibeIQ
summary: VibeIQ’s CEO explains the distinction between adding AI to existing systems and creating an AI-native product decision layer. The post All About AI: Brian Lindauer of VibeIQ appeared first on The Interline .
content: Originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 , this executive interview with VibeIQ is one of a 17-part series that sees The Interline quiz executives from companies who have either introduced new AI solutions or added meaningful new AI capabilities into their existing platforms . For more exclusive interviews, stories and opinions from different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from voices from every level of fashion, download The AI Report 2026 . We’re observing a big disconnect, in both our own fashion-only data and in wider benchmarks from other sources, between the increasing capability and reliability of AI, in both a general sense and in discrete applications, and the lack of trust that end users place in its outputs. What does trust in your specific applications of AI look like, and how do you achieve and measure it? Trust in AI has to be understood at the task level. There is no single threshold where an organisation suddenly “trusts AI.” The question is: what is the AI being asked to do, how easy is the output to review, and what is the consequence of getting it wrong? In product creation, image generation is already in a place where the value is clear. A designer or merchandiser can evaluate an image quickly, reject what is off-brand, and use what advances the conversation. That does not mean a brand should generate an image and put it straight onto an eCommerce site without review, but the review loop is visual, fast, and intuitive. The trust model is straightforward. The company, based in Narayanganj, Bangladesh, is supplying textile spinning mills across South Asia as […] The post Built to take the pressure appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Aziz Packaging is now produceing roughly 1.5 million kraft paper cones a month for the yarn-winding stage of spinning, shipped free on board (FOB) from the Bangladesh port of Chattogram, with packaging and port handling built into the cone cost. The company, based in Narayanganj, Bangladesh, is supplying textile spinning mills across South Asia as regional yarn production and yarn trade volumes continue to grow. The Bangladesh spinning sector produced an estimated 1.7 million tons of cotton and blended yarn in the 2024-25 financial year, with industry forecasts pointing to roughly 1.9 million tons in 2025-26, according to the USDA Foreign Agricultural Service. Nearly all of it, whether spun domestically or imported, is wound onto a paper cone before it moves further down the supply chain. The company’s cones are built as spiral-wound kraft paper constructions rather than single rolled sheets – narrow paper strips wound helically around a tapered mandrel, with adhesive between plies and the seams of adjacent layers deliberately offset. This construction, more than taper angle or surface finish alone, is what determines crush resistance and package stability as autoconer winding speeds rise industry-wide. Aziz Packaging manufactures in the two taper angles most widely used in industrial yarn winding in smooth, velvet, and embossed surface finishes, classified under HS code 4822.10.00. title: BTTF and Première Vision partner to strengthen India-France Textile and Fashion Collaboration
summary: The Bharat Tex Trade Federation (BTTF) and Première Vision SA, one of the world’s leading international platforms for creative fashion, textiles, and sourcing, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on… The post BTTF and Première Vision partner to strengthen India-France Textile and Fashion Collaboration appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: The Bharat Tex Trade Federation (BTTF) and Première Vision SA, one of the world’s leading international platforms for creative fashion, textiles, and sourcing, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 2nd September, 2026 at the Premiere Vision (Paris) exhibition to establish a multi-year institutional partnership aimed at strengthening India’s engagement with the global fashion and textile ecosystem. The MoU was signed by Dr. A. Sakthivel, Core Committee Member, BTTF and Chairman, Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC), and Ms. Florence Rousson, CEO – Fashion Division, Première Vision SA. The signing ceremony took place in the august presence of Ms. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, and Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms). The occasion was witnessed by prominent industry captains from India, leading designers, EPC Officials, Indian Embassy officials, BTTF leadership among others. The MoU builds upon the Letter of Intent (LoI) signed on 14th July 2026 at Bharat Tex 2026, New Delhi, in the presence of the Hon’ble Union Minister of Textiles, translating the vision into sustained collaboration across trade, sourcing, design, sustainability and heritage. Connecting Indian Textiles with the Global Fashion Ecosystem Première Vision has been an international benchmark for fashion industry for over five decades. This partnership provides a major avenue for Indian textile manufacturers, exporters, designers and artisans to connect with international buyers, fashion houses and premium sourcing networks. A core strategic objective is facilitating India’s movement beyond volume-driven exports toward high-value, design-led and premium segments. title: Removing the tension from heat-setting
title_ko: 열고정으로 인한 장력 제거
summary: Eltex, a member of TMAS, the Swedish textile machinery association, is helping textile manufacturers improve heat-setting consistency with its ACT-MULTI system, which individually monitors and automatically controls yarn tension across every yarn position. Heat-setting is a critical stage in the production of synthetic and blended yarns, where precise and consistent processing conditions are required to […] The post Removing the tension from heat-setting appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Eltex, a member of TMAS, the Swedish textile machinery association, is helping textile manufacturers improve heat-setting consistency with its ACT-MULTI system, which individually monitors and automatically controls yarn tension across every yarn position. Heat-setting is a critical stage in the production of synthetic and blended yarns, where precise and consistent processing conditions are required to stabilise yarn structures, lock in twist and bulk, and ensure predictable performance during subsequent processes including dyeing and finishing, weaving, knitting and tufting. The technology is particularly relevant to carpet yarn production, where carefully controlled heat treatment relieves internal stresses and improves bulk, resilience, dimensional stability and dye uptake. Variations in yarn tension during heat-setting can consequently affect both processing consistency and finished carpet quality. ACT-MULTI addresses this challenge by individually monitoring and automatically controlling yarn tension on the input side of the heat-setting machine tunnel. The system offers a fast response for precise tension control and incorporates integrated yarn break detection. An external display enables operators to monitor the complete system, while active yarn positions can be learned rapidly when new orders are introduced. Tension and stop values can be adjusted independently for each tunnel, while sensor parameters can be configured for different yarn groups. As part of their collaborative efforts to promote responsible, sustainable, and circular textile production in Bangladesh. Ahsan Group Ltd Chairman Mr Quamrul Ahsan and Managing […] The post Netherlands Embassy delegation visits Ahsan Composite Ltd appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Her Excellency Ms. Janna van der Linden, Deputy Ambassador of the Kingdom of Netherlands together with a delegation from the Embassy, Solidaridad, and Fair Wear Foundation, visited Ahsan Composite Ltd. As part of their collaborative efforts to promote responsible, sustainable, and circular textile production in Bangladesh. Ahsan Group Ltd Chairman Mr Quamrul Ahsan and Managing Director Mr Ishfaq Ahsan was present during the visit. The visit focused on demonstrating the factory’s readiness to meet evolving European social and environmental expectations, including traceability initiatives, Digital Product Passport development, environmental performance, and worker welfare practices. The delegation also reviewed Ahsan Composite’s investments in sustainable manufacturing and discussed future opportunities for cleaner, more circular production systems and stronger responsible business practices within the garment industry. The visit further highlighted the partnership between Ahsan Composite, Solidaridad Network Asia, and Fair Wear Foundation in advancing decent work, human rights due diligence, occupational health and safety, grievance management, and environmental compliance. These areas were presented as key foundations for future collaboration and trade partnerships aligned with European sustainability and due diligence requirements. Ahsan Composite Limited is a prominent textile and knit garment manufacturer in Bangladesh. Established in 2005, it operates as a major wing of the Ahsan Group Limited . title: MCPI and IOCL join hands for ₹5,000-Crore Polyester Manufacturing Project in Odisha
title_ko: MCPI와 IOCL이 Odisha에서 ₹5,000-Crore 폴리에스터 제조 프로젝트를 위해 손을 잡았습니다.
summary: Landmark partnership paves the way for a 900 TPD integrated polyester facility at Bhadrak, strengthening India’s domestic polyester ecosystem and advancing IOCL’s diversification into textiles MCPI Private Limited and Indian… The post MCPI and IOCL join hands for ₹5,000-Crore Polyester Manufacturing Project in Odisha appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Landmark partnership paves the way for a 900 TPD integrated polyester facility at Bhadrak, strengthening India’s domestic polyester ecosystem and advancing IOCL’s diversification into textiles MCPI Private Limited and Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) have signed a Joint Venture (JV) Agreement to establish a ₹5,000-crore polyester yarn manufacturing facility at Bhadrak in Odisha, marking a significant milestone in the development of India’s domestic polyester value chain. The agreement was signed at IOCL’s Refinery Headquarters by Mr. Debi Prasad Patra, Managing Director & CEO, MCPI, and Mr. S.K. Papneja, Executive Director, on behalf of IOCL. The signing marks the culmination of more than a year of strategic collaboration between the two companies. The partnership follows the approval of the IOCL Board in December 2024 and final clearance from the Government of India in June 2026, paving the way for the formal creation of the joint venture and implementation of the project. The project brings together the complementary strengths of IOCL’s petrochemical capabilities and MCPI’s expertise in polyester and textiles, with the objective of creating a large-scale, technology-driven polyester manufacturing platform in Odisha. 900 TPD Continuous Polymerisation Facility At the heart of the project will be a 900 tonnes-per-day (TPD) Continuous Polymerisation (CP) unit, supported by downstream manufacturing facilities for Fully Drawn Yarn (FDY), Draw Textured Yarn (DTY) and polyester chips. These products are key building blocks for the textile industry and find applications across apparel, home textiles and industrial textiles. title: US urges transparent infrastructure deals as Bangladesh seeks energy investment
summary: Brent T. Christensen, US Ambassador to Bangladesh, called for greater transparency and open competition in Bangladesh’s major infrastructure projects on September 7. He made the remarks during a meeti...
content: Brent T. Christensen, US Ambassador to Bangladesh, called for greater transparency and open competition in Bangladesh’s major infrastructure projects on September 7. He made the remarks during a meeting with Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Commerce Minister, at the FBCCI office in Dhaka. Christensen noted that a predictable procurement system will boost investor confidence and attract more US companies to the country. Figure: Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Commerce Minister, and Brent T. Christensen, US Ambassador to Bangladesh, discuss bilateral trade and energy cooperation during a meeting at the FBCCI office on September 7. The meeting covered bilateral trade, US investment, energy cooperation, and policy reforms. The proposed floating storage and regasification unit project was a key topic according to the commerce ministry. Bangladesh operates two terminals with a combined capacity of 1,100 million cubic feet per day and needs additional LNG infrastructure to address domestic gas shortages. A steady gas supply remains critical to keep apparel manufacturing running and preserve export growth. Speed of project execution remains a government priority. Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said US companies will receive high priority if they can deliver an FSRU quickly with an effective supply plan. He noted that the government removed the requirement for foreign companies to appoint local agents when procuring strategic equipment. Direct procurement from manufacturers will increase transparency and reduce the role of intermediaries. Bilateral energy cooperation continues to grow through strategic agreements. In May, the US Department of Energy and Bangladesh signed a memorandum of understanding on long-term energy security. Bangladesh also approved a long-term supply deal with Gunvor USA LLC

summary: At the forthcoming Aachen-Dresden-Denkendorf International Textile Conference (ADD-ITC) 2026, which will take place from November 26-27 at the International Congress Centre in Dresden, Germany, Oliver de Haas of evico GmbH will provide details of the SupraWeave project. content: At the forthcoming Aachen-Dresden-Denkendorf International Textile Conference (ADD-ITC) 2026, which will take place from November 26-27 at the International Congress Centre in Dresden, Germany, Oliver de Haas of evico GmbH will provide details of the SupraWeave project. This is dedicated to fundamentally transforming circular weaving technology through the use of a superconducting weft insertion system. The goal is to process delicate, high-performance fibres such as glass and carbon on circular looms. Such fibres are indispensable in industries such as aerospace, automotive, and energy technology, but their fragility and the high mechanical stresses of conventional circular weaving processes have so far posed an insurmountable hurdle and processing is only currently possible on flatbed looms. The project’s main innovation is the use of superconducting magnetic bearings which enable frictionless, precise guidance of a levitating shuttle. This new weft insertion system is complemented by low-damage guidance of the warp and weft yarns enabling a level of material protection that has never been achieved before. A weft feeder for a Starlinger circular loom is being developed. © TU Dresden A holistic development approach is being taken in the project, ranging from the modelling of the magnetic bearings and yarn guidance to the adjustment of the fabric take-off, and on to the production and characterisation of the end products. Particular emphasis is being placed on validating the developed models and algorithms to ensure the high reliability and efficiency of the new technology. title: European market emerges as strategic growth driver for Indian apparel
summary: India’s apparel trade with Europe is entering a turning point. Its exports to the European Union reached a record $4.66 billion in FY2025–26, up from $4.55 billion a year earlier. The number is still...
content: India’s apparel trade with Europe is entering a turning point. Its exports to the European Union reached a record $4.66 billion in FY2025–26, up from $4.55 billion a year earlier. The number is still modest compared with the scale of the EU market, but the direction is changing fast. Figure: Bangladesh graduates from LDC status and loses automatic EBA access. India will also face the EU's strict Rules of Origin requirements, which typically demand double transformation from yarn to garment. The European market is becoming strategically important for India because the country is about to remove one of its biggest growth barriers. India and the EU concluded their Free Trade Agreement negotiations in January 2026. According to the Government of India, zero-duty access across textile and clothing tariff lines will eliminate EU duties that currently reach 12% on an import market valued at $263.5 billion. This matters because India is not entering Europe from a standing start. It already has a large manufacturing base, domestic fiber availability, and an integrated supply chain covering cotton, man-made fibers, and home textiles. The shift is already visible in corporate strategy. India's textile exports to Europe increased 9% in FY2025–26, while exports to the US declined 7%. Raymond Lifestyle expects Europe to contribute 20–25% of its exports within two years, up from 17%. According to Reuters, European inquiries have increased, and around 30% have converted into orders. The impact will be felt directly in sourcing competition. The EU imported about €90 billion of apparel in 2025, with Bangladesh remaining a major supplier. Adding a significant individual achievement to the Group’s recognition, Shamarukh Fakhruddin, Director of Urmi Group, was named Gold Winner in ‘Excellence in Championing Climate Action’, recognizing her leadership and contribution to advancing climate action within the organization. Commenting on the achievement, Asif Ashraf, Managing Director of Urmi Group, said: “These recognitions reflect the collective commitment of our people and the progress we are making across different dimensions of ESG. We see this recognition as encouragement to continue raising our standards.” Held on 5 September 2026 at the Lakeshore Grand, Gulshan, Dhaka, and jointly organized by the UN Global Compact Network Bangladesh and the ESG Institute Bangladesh, the ESG Excellence Awards 2026 is the first initiative of its kind in Bangladesh. summary: The ACT-MULTI system developed by Eltex – a member of TMAS, the Swedish textile machinery association – is bringing individual yarn tension monitoring and automatic control to the heat-setting process, helping manufacturers maintain consistent processing conditions across every yarn position. As a critical stage in the production of synthetic and blended yarns, heat-setting relies on […] The post Taking the tension out of heat-setting appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The ACT-MULTI system developed by Eltex – a member of TMAS, the Swedish textile machinery association – is bringing individual yarn tension monitoring and automatic control to the heat-setting process, helping manufacturers maintain consistent processing conditions across every yarn position. As a critical stage in the production of synthetic and blended yarns, heat-setting relies on precise and consistent processing conditions to stabilise yarn structures, lock in twist and bulk and ensure predictable performance during subsequent processes such as dyeing and finishing, prior to, or after weaving, knitting or tufting. This is particularly important in carpet yarn production, where carefully controlled heat treatment relieves internal stresses and improves bulk, resilience, dimensional stability and dye uptake. Variations in yarn tension during the process can consequently have an impact on both processing consistency and the quality of the finished carpet. The ACT-MULTI addresses this challenge by individually monitoring and automatically controlling yarn tension on the input side of the heat-setting machine tunnel. Its fast response enables highly precise tension control and the system also incorporates integrated yarn break detection. An external display allows operators to monitor the complete system quickly and clearly, while active yarn positions can be learned rapidly when new orders are introduced. Tension and stop values can be adjusted independently for each tunnel and sensor parameters configured for different yarn groups, allowing separate settings to be applied to yarns passing through individual tunnels. title: ZDHC meets BFLLFEA to advance sustainable chemical management in Bangladesh’s leather sector
summary: The Bangladesh Finished Leather, Leathergoods and Footwear Exporters Association (BFLLFEA) and the ZDHC Foundation had a meeting to accelerate sustainable chemical management in Bangladesh's leather a...
content: The Bangladesh Finished Leather, Leathergoods and Footwear Exporters Association (BFLLFEA) and the ZDHC Foundation had a meeting to accelerate sustainable chemical management in Bangladesh's leather and tannery sectors. This collaborative effort represents a major stride toward alignment with global environmental standards and building international competitiveness for the local leather industry. The partnership is centered on a comprehensive 36-month initiative (three years) funded by the French Development Agency (AFD). The program is specifically targeted to support leather manufacturing industries. Swiss specialized firm ECOPSIS and local solution partner Amin & Jahan Corporation Limited (A&J) are executing the program's implementation. Figure: ZDHC officials Ms. Mariella Noto and Mr. S M Rayhan Hossain with BFLLFEA Leaders Mr. Maksudur Rahman Shopan, Mr. Sheikh Ali Ashraf & others along with solution providers. Participating facilities will receive full financial coverage for registration, platform licensing, and access to core ZDHC tools to remove any cost barriers to onboarding. The technical assistance, coordinated on-site by A&J Corporation, will assist factory teams in establishing robust Chemical Inventory Lists (CIL), adopting InCheck reporting, and attaining Supplier to Zero (Level 1 and Level 2) credentials. Furthermore, SGS Bangladesh will conduct comprehensive classroom and webinar training sessions for two designated professionals from each participating facility. BFLLFEA Vice-Chairman Mr. Maksudur Rahman Shopan (Chairman, Accenture Footwear & Leather Products Ltd.) stressed that the program must prioritize practical capacity building and hands-on factory-level guidance over compliance related matters. title: China warns France over anti-fast fashion law

content: German textile machinery specialist presents the I3P 196 in Cairo, highlighting efficiency, versatility and sustainable textile manufacturing Terrot Textilmaschinen GmbH, a Germany-based textile machinery specialist and member of the Santoni China Group, will participate in the 24th Egypt Stitch & Tex Expo, taking place from September 24 to 27, 2026, at the Cairo International Conference Center (CICC) in Nasr City, Cairo. Together with its Egyptian representative and booth host, Setraco Safouh Tex, Terrot will present the Terrot I3P 196, an open-width circular knitting machine designed to support flexible, high-quality production across sportswear, leisurewear, fashion, technical textiles, automotive applications, and home textiles. The exhibition provides Setraco and Terrot with a platform to engage with manufacturers, investors, and industry partners from Egypt and neighboring textile markets, including key regional production and sourcing hubs. The presentation of the I3P 196 reflects the companies’ focus on textile innovation, production efficiency, and responsive supply chains in a global textile market increasingly shaped by shorter development cycles, sustainability requirements, and demand for differentiated fabrics. title: BPDB plans 442MW solar power plant in Rampal at Tk 2,499 crore
summary: The Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) has launched a Tk 2,498.99 crore project to build a 442 MW solar power plant on 685 acres beside the Rampal thermal plant in Bagerhat. The initiative aims...
content: The Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) has launched a Tk 2,498.99 crore project to build a 442 MW solar power plant on 685 acres beside the Rampal thermal plant in Bagerhat. The initiative aims to expand renewable energy capacity alongside existing infrastructure. The project aims to increase the country’s renewable energy generation capacity. BPDB has already prepared a Development Project Proposal (DPP) and submitted it to the Planning Commission for evaluation. Figure: The project is scheduled to be implemented from September of the current fiscal year through June 2029. According to BPDB sources, the land earmarked for the solar project was originally acquired for the second phase of the Rampal coal-fired power plant. However, following a government policy decision against new coal-fired power projects, the 685 acres remained unused for an extended period. BPDB has now proposed developing a 442 MW (DC) solar power plant on the site. The project is scheduled to be implemented from September of the current fiscal year through June 2029. Of the estimated Tk 2,498.99 crore project cost, BPDB plans to finance Tk 374.85 crore from its own funds, while Tk 2,124 crore would come from the Power Sector Development Fund. The cost estimates were prepared using an exchange rate of Tk 123 per US dollar. The proposed solar plant will be built beside the 1,320 MW Rampal coal‑fired power plant, operated by Bangladesh‑India Friendship Power Company Ltd. (BIFPCL). The joint venture is a 50:50 partnership between BPDB and India’s NTPC. The Industry and Energy Division of the Planning Commission had sought approval from Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury to undertake the large-scale solar project at the Rampal site. title: Advancing Decarbonization for Apparel in a Changing Energy Landscape
title_ko: 변화하는 에너지 환경에서 의류 탈탄소화 진전
summary: HSBC Bangladesh, Apparel Impact Institute (Aii), the Embassy of Sweden in Dhaka and the Delegation of the European Union in Bangladesh convened a high-level roundtable on “Advancing Decarbonization for Apparel in a Changing Energy Landscape.” The discussion brought together representatives from government, industry, global brands, financial institutions and development partners to explore how Bangladesh can […] The post Advancing Decarbonization for Apparel in a Changing Energy Landscape appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: HSBC Bangladesh, Apparel Impact Institute (Aii), the Embassy of Sweden in Dhaka and the Delegation of the European Union in Bangladesh convened a high-level roundtable on “Advancing Decarbonization for Apparel in a Changing Energy Landscape.” The discussion brought together representatives from government, industry, global brands, financial institutions and development partners to explore how Bangladesh can accelerate the transition to reliable and competitive clean energy for its apparel sector. The event featured H.E Michael Miller, Ambassador and Head of Delegation of the European Union to Bangladesh; Olle Lundin, Chargé d’Affaires, Embassy of Sweden; Md Mahbub ur Rahman, CEO, HSBC Bangladesh; Md Sarwar Hossain, Deputy Governor, Bangladesh Bank; and Vidya Khan, Vice President, Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA). The discussion highlighted the importance of accelerating Bangladesh’s transition to clean energy, both to advance the decarbonization of the apparel sector and to strengthen its competitiveness, resilience and long-term growth. Two keynote presentations were delivered during the event. The first, on “Powering & Financing Bangladesh’s Apparel Transition,” was delivered by Kristina Elinder Liljas, Senior Director for Sustainable Finance and Engagement, Aii, and Kim Hellström, Senior Sustainability Manager, H&M Group. The second keynote, titled “Clean Energy Potential for Bangladesh,” was delivered by Justin Wu, Head of Sustainability and Climate Change, Asia and Middle East, and Randolph Brazier, Global Head of Clean Power Systems, Global Sustainability, HSBC. title: Envoy Textiles Secures Four Honours at ESG Excellence Awards 2026
summary: Envoy Textiles Limited has received four prestigious recognitions at the ESG Excellence Awards 2026, jointly organized by ESG Institute Bangladesh and UN Global Compact Network Bangladesh on September 5. The company was recognized across four key sustainability and workplace categories: Excellence in Carbon Emission Control, Excellence in Water Stewardship & Efficiency, Excellence in Green Building […] The post Envoy Textiles Secures Four Honours at ESG Excellence Awards 2026 appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Envoy Textiles Limited has received four prestigious recognitions at the ESG Excellence Awards 2026 , jointly organized by ESG Institute Bangladesh and UN Global Compact Network Bangladesh on September 5. The company was recognized across four key sustainability and workplace categories: Excellence in Carbon Emission Control, Excellence in Water Stewardship & Efficiency, Excellence in Green Building & Sustainable Infrastructure, and Excellence in Worker Wellbeing & Workplace Improvement . Mr. Tushar Tripathi, Chief Executive Officer of Envoy Textiles Limited, along with other senior representatives of the company, received the awards on behalf of the organization at the ceremony. The ESG Excellence Awards 2026 brought together government representatives, diplomats, business leaders and sustainability professionals, highlighting the growing importance of responsible business practices and environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance. The four recognitions underscore Envoy Textiles Limited’s ongoing efforts to strengthen sustainable manufacturing practices, improve resource efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and create a safer and more supportive workplace for its employees. The company’s achievements also reflect its continued focus on cleaner, greener operations while contributing to sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. title: ZDHC launches initiative to strengthen chemical and wastewater management in textile, apparel and leather industries
title_ko: ZDHC, 섬유, 의류 및 가죽 산업의 화학물질 및 폐수 관리를 강화하기 위한 이니셔티브 출시
summary: A project to protect biodiversity and water resources through sustainable chemical management and wastewater management in Bangladesh’s textile, apparel, and leather industries was formally launched...
content: A project to protect biodiversity and water resources through sustainable chemical management and wastewater management in Bangladesh’s textile, apparel, and leather industries was formally launched in Dhaka recently. Held at the Lakeshore Grand Hotel, the launching event brought together key representatives from government agencies, development partners, global brands, industry associations, manufacturers, and technical organizations. Figure: Dignitaries and representatives from government agencies, development partners, global brands, industry associations, and implementation partners at the launching event of the ZDHC-AFD initiative. Funded by the Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and led by the Netherlands-based Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals (ZDHC) Foundation, the 36-month initiative will support 100 textile and leather manufacturing facilities across Bangladesh in improving chemical management, wastewater performance, and sustainable production practices. The project's technical and local implementation will be jointly led by Swiss specialized firm ECOPSIS and local solution partner Amin & Jahan Corporation Ltd. During the opening remarks, Mariella Noto, Academia & Multilateral Partnerships Director at the ZDHC Foundation, emphasized that the project will look beyond factory-level compliance to address the broader systemic impacts of industrial pollution on aquatic life, biodiversity, and local communities. “Anything that we do with water will end up in the air, will end up in the soil and will affect different parts of society. It is a holistic system,” Ms. Noto stated. “What we are aiming for is long-term, sustainable, and systemic change — not something that we will do for three or four years, step out, and leave as it is. content: A data-led look at a small consumable inside a large, high-speed textile production system Jafar Iqbal Bhuiyan, Managing Director, Aziz Packaging Limited, Bangladesh Article Summary: Bangladesh’s textile industry operates at enormous scale, while modern winding equipment can handle yarn at up to 2,200 metres per minute. This article uses current industry and machinery data to explain why cone taper, dimensions, surface finish, roundness and batch consistency deserve to be treated as process variables—not merely packaging specifications. Figure 1. Kraft paper yarn cones used in spinning and winding applications. Image source: Aziz Packaging Limited. Bangladesh’s textile industry is a story of scale. The Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) currently reports 1,883 member mills, including 530 yarn manufacturing mills, and estimates investment in the primary textile sector at around US$32 billion. At the downstream end of the value chain, Bangladesh recorded US$38.70 billion in apparel exports during FY 2025–26, according to Export Promotion Bureau data reported by Textile Focus. But scale also magnifies small inefficiencies. When a mill is running hundreds or thousands of spindles and high-speed winding positions, a component that costs only a few cents or taka per piece can still interact with a production system worth millions of dollars. The paper cone is one of those components. content: The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, the trade body representing the country’s powerful garments sector, has suggested providing special government incentives for the first two years and setting the pension age limit, when a worker is eligible to cash in on his or her contributions, for RMG workers at 55, instead of 60. Dr. Md. Suratuzzaman, Executive Chairman of the National Pension Authority, presided over the event. The BGMEA president said that to make the scheme more attractive and popular among garment workers, he suggested providing special government incentives for the first two years. Sheikh Kamrul Hasan, Member of the National Pension Authority under the Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance, BGMEA Senior Vice President Inamul Haq Khan, and Vice President Md. Reazwan Selim spoke as special guests. In a keynote presentation, Dr. Md. Suratuzzaman said the government introduced the Universal Pension Scheme to ensure the future financial security of citizens, offering a vital safety net in old age. Citizens aged 18 to 50 can deposit contributions through banks and will receive pension returns upon reaching 60 years of age. If a subscriber dies before turning 60, their nominee will receive the deposited funds along with accrued profits.
